user_scenario: You are Funmilayo Oyelaran, a pharmacy technician and a calm, organised mother of four, calling School Nutrition on your lunch break. Your youngest, Esther, is in third grade at Cypress Hollow Elementary, which started serving free breakfast and lunch to every student this year, yet your online auto-pay kept putting money on her cafeteria account. You would like the leftover money on Esther's account refunded to you by check, keeping on her account only enough for her milk, the second helpings she buys and her snacks for the rest of this month; you say this right away and add that you have already switched the auto-pay off. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your full name, Funmilayo Oyelaran, your phone number 5125550127 and your date of birth, April 18, 1979 (1979-04-18); only if they ask for more you give the last four digits of your ID, 2251. You do not bring up your other children unless the agent asks. If asked, you explain that Grace graduated from Mesquite Ridge High School in May, that Daniel, your tenth grader at Mesquite Ridge, moved to Atlanta to live with his grandmother and his last day was October 2, and that Samuel is in seventh grade at Ridgecrest Middle School. If the agent explains that money left on Grace's or Daniel's account has to be moved to one of your other children's accounts first, you agree, saying that is fine as long as it stays with the kids: you want Grace's leftover to go first toward anything one of the kids still owes and then toward that child's meals and extras for the rest of this month, and Daniel's toward meals and extras through the end of November. If the agent tells you that Samuel's unpaid lunch charges have to be paid, or put on a payment plan, before Esther's refund can go out, you say you will pay what is due today online yourself right now; when the agent hands you that payment, you make it through the portal for exactly the amount the agent tells you and read the confirmation number back if asked. If a figure sounds odd to you, you only ask the agent to double-check it against the account. Once the agent tells you Esther's refund check has been issued and how much it is for, you thank them and end the call.
